page: Microsoft Azure E20s_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 10 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The CPU architecture includes an allocation of 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 480 MB L3 cache. Modern vector and matrix instruction extensions are supported, including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX (tile and int8), alongside cryptographic accelerators such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The system is equipped with 160.0 GB of system memory, delivering a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Memory subsystem throughput reaches 139.09 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 57.2 GB/sec for large-block writes. There is no bundled local storage included with the instance, requiring network-attached storage via Azure Premium Storage for persistent file and disk operations. The virtual machine also does not include discrete GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations highlight strong performance in compression routines, recording 35.43 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 14.68 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression, both placing within the top quartile. Small-model language inference exhibits top-tier text generation throughput at 364.6 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model. General compute metrics, such as PassMark CPU at 33,289.29 and multi-core stress-ng at 20,536.75, fall within standard mid-range distributions, alongside Redis SET performance measuring 34.54 million operations per second.

Given its 8:1 memory footprint and high single-core compression speeds, the E20s_v7 provides a balanced resource cost profile for memory-bound applications without the overhead of unused local NVMe disks. It is appropriately suited for relational and in-memory database engines, caching layers, data transformation pipelines, and enterprise enterprise resource planning workloads.
